title: Incremental release orchestration - cross-functional playbook (notes)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working notes doc for an end-to-end incremental release orchestration pattern that combines small canaries, targeted A/B slices, and automatic safety gates. Goal: give ENG/Product/RELIABILITY/CS a concise checklist and operational model to reduce cognitive load during rollouts while preserving the ability to stop fast.

Audience:
- Product and PMs running feature experiments that affect inference models/routing
- SRE and Serving Runtime teams responsible for latency/cost SLOs
- Solutions/CS for customer-facing changes and communication
- Developer experience/console team for rollout UI requirements

High level summary (one-paragraph):
Use a staged release with 4 phases (probe -> canary -> ramp -> full) + an A/B control plane for experiments. Each phase has explicit signals (performance, correctness, economics) and a short checklist. Implement an experiment metadata contract so every request can be traced back to model/revision/route/prompt-template. Automate the easy aborts and leave judgment calls to humans for ambiguous regressions.

Definitions / phases (quick):
- Probe (0.1% synthetic or internal): smoke on non-customer traffic; run synthetic prompts + internal eval set; verify no immediate errors; duration: 15–60m
- Canary (1%–5%): small slice of real users or a representative cohort; monitor safety signals closely; autoscale measured; duration: 1–24h depending on signal quality
- Ramp (5%–50%): incremental increases (5x each step or linear) with short hold windows; verify long-tail metrics; duration: multi-day typically
- Full (100%): rollout complete; keep a tighter monitoring window for 72h post-full

Traffic allocation patterns (practical):
- Random uniform sampling for low-risk features (UI text tweak).
- Stratified/cohort sampling for model changes that are sensitive to locale, device type, or route. E.g., pick 3 high-traffic and 2 low-traffic cohorts for canary to surface interaction effects.
- Customer-targeted slices for enterprise customers (explicit opt-in for private deployments).

Cohort selection checklist:
- representativity: includes mobile/desktop, top-3 geos, first-time users vs returning
- tenancy: avoid putting >2 high-importance accounts in one canary slice
- instrumentation coverage: all cohorts must have active tracing and perf-tagging

Signals and metrics to watch (must be instrumented):
- Reliability: error rate (4xx/5xx), API timeouts, uncaught exceptions (alerts at +3x baseline), retries/sec
- Latency: median, p95, p99 (token generation and end-to-end response), cold-starts/sec
- Cost/throughput: tokens/sec, cost-per-request estimate, GPU utilization (for Dedicated), batch size distribution
- Quality/regression: automated prompt-set quality delta (embedding-similarity/ BLEU-like proxy), hallucination heuristic rate, semantic-fidelity score from eval harness
- Business KPIs: conversion rate, CTR, revenue impact (if measurable)

Thresholds / abort gates (examples to calibrate per-product):
- Immediate abort: error rate > baseline + 5 percentage points AND absolute error rate > 1% over 5m
- Soft hold: p95 latency > baseline * 1.5 for 15m OR cost-per-token > budgeted threshold for 30m
- Quality flag: automated eval failure on golden prompt-set (precision drop > 4%) -> hold and notify product + research
- Risk budget exhaustion: if cumulative risk budget for the week is consumed (see risk budget calculation below) -> stop ramps until review

Rollback and mitigation playbook (short):
1) Stop traffic to variant and route to fallback model (auto if configured).
2) Open incident channel #rollout-incidents and post rollout metadata (model/revision/commit, traffic slice ids, start times).
3) Run targeted diagnostics: top-N error traces, p95 by cohort, recent deploys overlapping window.
4) If business impact visible, escalate to on-call SRE + PM for decision to rollback or quick fix.
5) Postmortem template: timeline, root cause hypothesis, customer impact, and immediate follow-ups.

Observability checklist and quick queries (console needs these panels pre-baked):
- Error-rate heatmap by route and cohort (last 60m, 6h, 72h)
- Latency waterfall: client->edge->runtime->gpu (p50/p95/p99)
- Eval-regression dashboard: golden prompt-set score trend and per-prompt diffs
- Cost estimator: projected spend delta for next 24h at current traffic
- Canary slice breakdown: cohort membership, churn, top versions seen by that slice
- Trace sample link: from a failed request to full trace, request payload and model revision

Experiment metadata contract (critical):
Every request must carry:
- experiment_id or rollout_id
- model_id and model_revision (semantic version string)
- quant_profile (e.g., q4_0/q8_1) and runtime_variant (gpu/cpu/quant)
- prompt_template_id, prompt_hash
- cohort_id and allocation_seed
- origin (sdk/http/console)
Why: enables deterministic reconstruction of regressions, automatic grouping in dashboards, and linking to CI/PR that produced the revision.

Risk budget concept (short primer):
- Allocate a small weekly risk budget as "acceptable regression exposure" for the product team (units: % of shifted traffic-minutes or an expected number of failures).
- Each canary/ramp step consumes budget proportional to observed signal deltas and slice size.
- When budget hits zero, no new ramps allowed without explicit exec-level sign-off.

Automation ideas (low effort -> high impact):
- Auto-route fallback when immediate abort conditions met (configurable per-route)
- Canary smoke runner: small synthetic suite that runs against every new revision automatically at probe stage
- Rollout template generator in Console: take inputs (slices, metrics, thresholds) -> create rollout with prewired dashboards and incident channel

Handoff and communication protocol (ceremony):
- Pre-launch: 30m sync with Product/ENG/SRE/CS. Share rollout plan + primary/backup contacts.
- Start: post in #deployments and tag on-call, link to console rollout object.
- Mid-rollout checkpoint: brief async note at each hold window (auto from Console).
- Abort/rollback: must include root-cause hypothesis + immediate next steps; SRE to file incident and PM to advise customer comms if needed.

Sample minimum checklist (for the person running rollout):
- [ ] Rollout object created in Console with metadata
- [ ] Dashboards linked and smoke tests passing
- [ ] Cohorts defined and instrumented
- [ ] Risk budget checked and approved
- [ ] Contact list posted in deploy channel
- [ ] Post-deploy monitoring window scheduled (72h)

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to represent multi-model rollouts (chain of rerankers + generator) in a single rollout object? TODO: propose schema for model graph.
- Fine-grained risk budget math (unit tests + simulation). Diego to simulate using last 6 months of traffic.
- Should cost gates be enforced automatically for Dedicated customers? Ops/legal implications.
- UX: what minimal fields must Console expose so non-engineering PM can create a safe rollout?

Related links and tickets:
- Confluence: rollout-framework-v2 (linked above)
- Jira: JIRA-RI-8721 (rollout metadata schema)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/release-playbooks/pull/129 (templates for Console)

Notes to self / rough ideas (choppy):
- consider a lightweight "experiment token" to mark user sessions (makes cohort continuity easier)
- split quality signal into application-specific and model-specific buckets (helps decide who owns the regression)
- short experiments (1–2h) for UI-only tweaks; always GA in probe->canary pattern for model changes
- next step: draft API for rollout objects + sample JSON, wire up to demo Console page

If you're reading and want to improve: add real threshold numbers for your product, and drop in the golden prompt-set for automated evals. Ping me (avery) for pairing on the Console sketch or the risk-budget sim.

-- end of working notes --
